questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to visit Australia and this was the perfect opportunity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Melbourne is a wonderful city to live and i highly recommend the city for an exchange trip. However beware that monash university (Clayton faculty) is an hours train ride from melbourne centrum. If you study computer science like i did, also beware that you probably won't be studying with australiens as the majority of fellow students will be from Asia or india, and approximately 30% of them are not able to speak english. Therefore you might be put in a study group with someone that is not able to speak english (like i did) and therefore are very hard to collaborate with.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Monash University is very good at giving you the relevant information and assistance if needed when arriving.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was pretty easy, but takes an effort. My recommendation (what i did) is to rent an airbnb for the first two weeks and find an apartment for the rest of the stay while you are in Melbourne. We found a company called: "Apartment living Melbourne" through the platform flatmates, which had a bunch of really nice apartments. But you will need to find roommates if this is your plan. I had three roommates and we managed to get a wonderful and big apartment in the middle of Melbourne on the 41th floor. 

My strongest recommendation is that you DO NOT take the housing that Monash provides or any other private provider like Unilodge, as this is at least double the price of what i paid for the luxury apartment described above and the apartments are VERY small.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It takes an effort, but is definitely worth it!

You won´t be able to get any good apartments from home, as you will need to show up for inspections.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is not very hard, but i had multiple assignments and Quiz´every week that did take a lot of time.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses are not hard to complete but the assignments does take a lot of time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The facilities are very good and teachers are also mostly good. However be prepared for icebreakers with fellow students in the first two weeks. Also there is a lot more group works, and the teachers will expect active participants during most lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I took these courses which dont have an exam, but the downside is you will be spending significant time on assignments and take at home quiz´s
1. FIT5057 - Project management
2. FIT5047 - Fundamentals of artificial intelligence
3. IT5147 - Data exploration and visualization
4. FIT5152 - User interface design and usability

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I can recommend these courses: 
FIT5057 - Project management
FIT5047 - Fundamentals of artificial intelligence
IT5147 - Data exploration and visualization

However stay away from this course as it is well below academic standards at UCPH: 
FIT5152 - User interface design and usability

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs. But you probably will spend a lot of money on going out with fellow students during the first couple of months and Alcohol is the only thing that is more expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Daily shopping and going out for food is probably 25-30% cheaper than Denmark. 
Clothes is also very cheap, so you might want to pack light and buy new clothes while you are there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There was a club for everything, however i did not sign up to any clubs as i lived 1 hour from campus. 
I did however use the tennis courts at the clayton campus frequently as they are very cheap. Between 12-14 o´clock they cost 12 kr. pr. hour.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything that you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I heard from fellow students that monash has a really good surfing/snowboarding club that arranges surfing and snowboarding trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city. Use the app Turo for car hire and go on hikes, Mornington peninsula and Philips island are good options. I did road trips in a campervan on the west coast and the east coast of Australia, which is a must do!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, but beware that in central Melbourne and at monash it will be hard to locate any local Australians as most people are foreign students from Asia or India which does affect the local culture in Melbourne.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say yes to every opportunity.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No particular challenge.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How easy going and friendly the Aussies are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Explore Australia, it is an amazing country. 
2. Socialize with fellow students. 
3. Don´t stay at Monash student accommodation or Unilodge.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is possible to take a lot of the courses online if that is what you want. Monash clayton campus is an hour in train from the center of Melbourne, so it can be a good option.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring Australia and meeting new people and cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was having four courses without exams but a lot of assignments and Quiz´s. It was not academically difficult, but they took up a lot of time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
